| [ADR](../adrs.md) | [Nygard, *Documenting Architecture Decisions*](https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions) (2011), with the summary line from [Zimmermann's Y-statement](https://ozimmer.ch/practices/2020/04/27/ArchitectureDecisionMaking.html) | Nygard's Context / Decision / Consequences, his four status values, and the rule that a reversed decision is superseded and left standing. The block-quote under the title states Zimmermann's six moves. A mandatory *Alternatives Considered* section matches [MADR 4](https://adr.github.io/madr/), which also asks for the options weighed | Nygard scopes a decision to one codebase. An ADR here affects more than one repository. Every alternative states a verdict, and *Consequences* is required where MADR leaves it optional. A fifth status, `rejected`, keeps a proposal the team turned down. A supersession is a pair of fields checked both ways, not a phrase inside the status. MADR's *Confirmation* is a separate type here: a standard cites the ADR it distils, and a control checks the standard. MADR's `consulted` and `informed` are not kept |
